problem: End-to-end learned policies for object search and navigation need many environment interactions and ignore the spatial semantic structure of indoor scenes (e.g., books on tables, plates in cupboards). It is also unclear which object embeddings best capture spatial proximity for search.
motivation: Humans find small objects in unseen houses by looking for larger co-located objects that are likely to hold them. Encoding such spatial priors in reusable object embeddings should give a sample-efficient, modular component that plugs into a classical mapping and planning pipeline.
key_idea: Use object embeddings (pre-trained word embeddings, or knowledge-graph embeddings trained on AI2Thor co-location relations) to rank visible large objects by similarity to the query, and greedily navigate to the best one with A* in partial-plan steps.
insight: Graph-based embeddings (RoboCSE, DeepWalk graph embedding) beat the word embeddings mainly when the target is far from the start (l>=20). For example, in the Kitchen, RoboCSE gets SPL 0.867 versus 0.573 for FastText and 0.581 for Word2Vec, while short-range cases are comparable. The authors' hypothesis is that at short range any action tends to move closer to the target, so spatial priors matter more for long searches. General-purpose text embeddings (Word2Vec, FastText) are a surprisingly strong baseline. There is no ablation of the beta partial-plan heuristic, and the appendix says oscillations were merely negligible.
method: Similarity-based sub-goal selection: at each step, list unvisited large objects (>1% of image area) in the 360° view and pick the one whose embedding has highest (cosine) similarity to the query embedding.

Momentum-like partial-plan execution: plan with A* to the sub-goal, execute only a fraction beta<1 of the plan (STEP MULTIPLE=5 steps of 0.25), then rescan and re-rank; this cuts compute per navigation and reduces oscillation between sub-goals.
Pre-trained word embeddings: off-the-shelf Word2Vec (Google News) and FastText (English Wikipedia), unmodified.
RoboCSE knowledge-base embeddings: multi-relational embeddings learned with the ANALOGY semantic-matching model from AI2Thor object metadata.

Graph Embedding: build a knowledge graph of object co-location and relations from AI2Thor floor plans per room type, treat all relations as equivalent (undirected), and run DeepWalk (20 walks, length 8, window 3) to get 25-d embeddings; frozen during navigation.
Task and perception assumptions: perfect object detection once an object occupies >=1% of pixels; success means seeing the object and being within about 5x0.25 units of it.

setting.backbone: Word2Vec / FastText (pre-trained, frozen); RoboCSE (ANALOGY) and DeepWalk graph embeddings (trained); A* planner
setting.training_data: Graph embeddings trained on knowledge graphs from a subset of AI2Thor floor plans per room type; Word2Vec on Google News, FastText on en Wikipedia; RoboCSE on AI2Thor metadata
setting.observation: 360° field of view with perfect object detection of large objects (>1% of image area); ground-truth object visibility, no vision-based mapping
setting.action_space: A* path to sub-goal, executed in steps of 0.25 units (5 steps per time step)
setting.privileged: Perfect object detection and ground-truth object identities; A* planning over a known navigable map

numbers.evidence: Table 1, Kitchen, Graph Embedding: 0.992 / 0.639 (SR shown as 0-1)

numbers_note: Results are on a custom AI2Thor object-search task, not a standard benchmark. Values are printed as fractions (0-1) and copied as is. Only two embedding variants are listed for brevity; the table also has RoboCSE/FastText/Word2Vec for all four room types. The split is unspecified in the paper.
results: All four embeddings reach SR of about 0.91-0.998 across room types, with SPL of about 0.62-0.70. Graph-based embeddings are clearly better on long paths (Kitchen l>=20 SPL: RoboCSE 0.867 vs Word2Vec 0.581), and are roughly equal to Word2Vec/FastText on short paths. Differences overall are small, and there is no non-semantic baseline (e.g., random or nearest-object) in the table.
limitations: Assumes perfect object detection and a known map for A*, with no vision-based perception or mapping.

Single simulator (AI2Thor) with only a few embedding types and no non-semantic baseline; differences between embeddings are small and no statistical significance is given. Only one random seed (33) is reported.
The oscillation-mitigation heuristic is not ablated or proven to remove oscillations; it only appeared negligible; multi-object queries are left to future work.
